title: How Was Madeira Formed? The Volcanic Story Behind the Cliffs and Coves
description: How Madeira was formed: a volcano rising from the Atlantic floor, carved into 580 m cliffs, sea caves and fajãs. See the geology up close from the sea.
heroAlt: Madeira's dramatic green sea cliffs seen from the Atlantic

images.prompt: Wide landscape photograph of Madeira's steep green and dark basalt sea cliffs on the south coast rising from deep blue Atlantic water, soft late-afternoon light, taken from a small boat.
images.alt: Madeira's volcanic sea cliffs rising from the Atlantic

images.prompt: Close photograph of the layered basalt cliff face of Cabo Girão in Madeira, showing dark lava layers and reddish ash bands, seen from the water below in clear daylight.
images.alt: Layers of lava and ash in the Cabo Girão cliff face

images.prompt: Photograph of Fajã dos Padres on Madeira's south coast, a small green flat platform at the foot of a tall cliff with a pebble shore and turquoise sea, seen from a small white private motorboat.
images.alt: Fajã dos Padres, a small platform below the cliffs
